passages.text: Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to His disciples: “The scribes and Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the crowds.
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said these words to them.
The scribes sit in Moses’ seat.
The Pharisees also sit in Moses’ seat.
Moses’ seat is a place of teaching and authority over the law.
passages.original: Τότε ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐλάλησεν τοῖς ὄχλοις καὶ τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ λέγων Ἐπὶ τῆς Μωϋσέως καθέδρας ἐκάθισαν οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι

passages.text: So practice and observe everything they tell you. But do not do what they do, for they do not practice what they preach.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the crowds and to His disciples.
The scribes and Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat.
They teach the law of Moses.
Do everything they tell you.
Obey their teaching.
But do not follow their actions.
They say things, but they do not do them.
passages.original: πάντα οὖν ὅσα ἐὰν εἴπωσιν ὑμῖν ποιήσατε καὶ τηρεῖτε κατὰ δὲ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν μὴ ποιεῖτε λέγουσιν γὰρ καὶ οὐ ποιοῦσιν

passages.text: They tie up heavy, burdensome loads and lay them on men’s shoulders, but they themselves are not willing to lift a finger to move them.
passages.sermon:
The scribes and Pharisees are religious leaders.
They tie up heavy loads.
These loads are hard to carry.
They place these loads on people’s shoulders.
They do not help others carry these loads.
They will not lift a finger to move them.
passages.original: δεσμεύουσιν δὲ φορτία βαρέα καὶ δυσβάστακτα καὶ ἐπιτιθέασιν ἐπὶ τοὺς ὤμους τῶν ἀνθρώπων αὐτοὶ δὲ τῷ δακτύλῳ αὐτῶν οὐ θέλουσιν κινῆσαι αὐτά

passages.text: All their deeds are done for men to see. They broaden their phylacteries and lengthen their tassels.
passages.sermon:
These people do everything to be seen by others.
They want people to notice their actions.
They make their phylacteries wide.
They make their tassels long.
passages.original: Πάντα δὲ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν ποιοῦσιν πρὸς τὸ θεαθῆναι τοῖς ἀνθρώποις πλατύνουσιν γὰρ τὰ φυλακτήρια αὐτῶν καὶ μεγαλύνουσιν τὰ κράσπεδα

passages.text: They love the places of honor at banquets, the chief seats in the synagogues, the greetings in the marketplaces, and the title of ‘Rabbi’ by which they are addressed.
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees are religious leaders.
They love places of honor at banquets.
They want the best seats in the synagogues.
They enjoy being greeted in the marketplaces.
They like to be called ‘Rabbi’ by other people.
passages.original: φιλοῦσιν δὲ τὴν πρωτοκλισίαν ἐν τοῖς δείπνοις καὶ τὰς πρωτοκαθεδρίας ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ τοὺς ἀσπασμοὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς καὶ καλεῖσθαι ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων Ῥαββί

passages.text: But you are not to be called ‘Rabbi,’ for you have one Teacher, and you are all brothers.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He warned them about seeking honor from people.
He said, “Do not let anyone call you ‘Rabbi.’”
You have only one Teacher.
All of you are brothers.
passages.original: Ὑμεῖς δὲ μὴ κληθῆτε Ῥαββί εἷς γάρ ἐστιν ὑμῶν ὁ διδάσκαλος πάντες δὲ ὑμεῖς ἀδελφοί ἐστε

passages.text: And do not call anyone on earth your father, for you have one Father, who is in heaven.
passages.sermon: Do not call anyone on earth your father.\r\nYou have one Father.\r\nYour Father is in heaven.
passages.original: καὶ πατέρα μὴ καλέσητε ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς εἷς γάρ ἐστιν ὑμῶν ὁ Πατὴρ ὁ οὐράνιος

passages.text: Nor are you to be called instructors, for you have one Instructor, the Christ.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He gave them instructions about titles and authority.
He said, “Do not let people call you instructors.”
You have only one Instructor.
Your Instructor is Christ.
passages.original: μηδὲ κληθῆτε καθηγηταί ὅτι καθηγητὴς ὑμῶν ἐστιν εἷς ὁ Χριστός

passages.text: The greatest among you shall be your servant.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He taught them about true greatness.
The greatest person among you must serve others.
A truly great person becomes your servant.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ μείζων ὑμῶν ἔσται ὑμῶν διάκονος

passages.text: For whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples and the crowds.
He taught about pride and humility.
If a person lifts himself up, God will bring him down.
If a person lowers himself, God will lift him up.
passages.original: Ὅστις δὲ ὑψώσει ἑαυτὸν ταπεινωθήσεται καὶ ὅστις ταπεινώσει ἑαυτὸν ὑψωθήσεται

passages.text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You shut the kingdom of heaven in men’s faces. You yourselves do not enter, nor will you let in those who wish to enter.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the scribes and Pharisees.
The scribes and Pharisees were religious leaders.
Jesus called them hypocrites.
He said, "Woe to you."
You shut the kingdom of heaven in front of people.
You do not enter the kingdom yourselves.
You do not allow those who want to enter to go in.
passages.original: Οὐαὶ δὲ ὑμῖν γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί ὅτι κλείετε τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων ὑμεῖς γὰρ οὐκ εἰσέρχεσθε οὐδὲ τοὺς εἰσερχομένους ἀφίετε εἰσελθεῖν

passages.text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You traverse land and sea to win a single convert, and when he becomes one, you make him twice as much a son of hell as you are.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the scribes and Pharisees.
The scribes and Pharisees were religious leaders.
They were hypocrites.
Jesus said, “Woe to you.”
You travel across land and sea.
You do this to make one convert.
When you succeed, you make that person a son of hell.
He becomes twice as much a son of hell as you are.
passages.original: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί ὅτι περιάγετε τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ τὴν ξηρὰν ποιῆσαι ἕνα προσήλυτον καὶ ὅταν γένηται ποιεῖτε αὐτὸν υἱὸν γεέννης διπλότερον ὑμῶν

passages.text: Woe to you, blind guides! You say, ‘If anyone swears by the temple, it means nothing; but if anyone swears by the gold of the temple, he is bound by his oath.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the scribes and Pharisees.
He called them blind guides.
He said they lead others but cannot see the truth themselves.
He rebuked them for their teaching about oaths.
They said, “If anyone swears by the temple, it means nothing.”
They also said, “If anyone swears by the gold of the temple, he is bound by his oath.”
They valued the gold more than the temple itself.
They taught people to honor the gold above the place that makes it holy.
passages.original: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν ὁδηγοὶ τυφλοὶ οἱ λέγοντες Ὃς ἂν ὀμόσῃ ἐν τῷ ναῷ οὐδέν ἐστιν ὃς δ’ ἂν ὀμόσῃ ἐν τῷ χρυσῷ τοῦ ναοῦ ὀφείλει

passages.text: You blind fools! Which is greater: the gold, or the temple that makes it sacred?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the scribes and Pharisees.
He called them blind fools.
He asked them a question.
He said, "Which is greater?"
He said, "Is the gold greater?"
He said, "Or is the temple greater?"
He said, "The temple makes the gold sacred."
passages.original: μωροὶ καὶ τυφλοί τίς γὰρ μείζων ἐστίν ὁ χρυσὸς ἢ ὁ ναὸς ὁ ἁγιάσας τὸν χρυσόν

passages.text: And you say, ‘If anyone swears by the altar, it means nothing; but if anyone swears by the gift on it, he is bound by his oath.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the religious leaders.
He called them blind guides.
He described their teaching about oaths.
They said, "If anyone swears by the altar, it means nothing."
They also said, "If anyone swears by the gift on the altar, he is bound by his oath."
They made a difference between the altar and the gift on it.
They taught that swearing by the altar was not important.
They taught that swearing by the gift on the altar was important.
They said a person must keep an oath made by the gift on the altar.
They said a person did not need to keep an oath made by the altar itself.
passages.original: καί Ὃς ἂν ὀμόσῃ ἐν τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ οὐδέν ἐστιν ὃς δ’ ἂν ὀμόσῃ ἐν τῷ δώρῳ τῷ ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ ὀφείλει

passages.text: You blind men! Which is greater: the gift, or the altar that makes it sacred?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the religious leaders.
He called them blind men.
He said, "You do not see the truth."
He asked them a question.
He said, "Which is greater?"
He gave two choices.
He said, "Is the gift greater?"
He said, "Or is the altar greater?"
He explained the altar makes the gift holy.
The altar gives the gift its sacred value.
passages.original: τυφλοί τί γὰρ μεῖζον τὸ δῶρον ἢ τὸ θυσιαστήριον τὸ ἁγιάζον τὸ δῶρον

passages.text: So then, he who swears by the altar swears by it and by everything on it.
passages.sermon: A person may make an oath by the altar.\r\nThis person swears by the altar itself.\r\nThis person also swears by everything placed on the altar.
passages.original: ὁ οὖν ὀμόσας ἐν τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ ὀμνύει ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐν πᾶσι τοῖς ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ

passages.text: And he who swears by the temple swears by it and by the One who dwells in it.
passages.sermon:
The temple is God's house.
God dwells in the temple.
If a person swears by the temple, he swears by the temple itself.
He also swears by God, who lives in the temple.
passages.original: καὶ ὁ ὀμόσας ἐν τῷ ναῷ ὀμνύει ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐν τῷ κατοικοῦντι αὐτόν

passages.text: And he who swears by heaven swears by God’s throne and by the One who sits on it.
passages.sermon:
A person may swear by heaven.
He swears by the throne of God.
He also swears by the One who sits on God’s throne.
God sits on His throne in heaven.
passages.original: καὶ ὁ ὀμόσας ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ὀμνύει ἐν τῷ θρόνῳ τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ ἐν τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You pay tithes of mint, dill, and cumin. But you have disregarded the weightier matters of the law: justice, mercy, and faithfulness. You should have practiced the latter, without neglecting the former.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the scribes and Pharisees.
The scribes and Pharisees were religious leaders.
Jesus called them hypocrites.
He said, “Woe to you.”
You pay tithes of mint.
You pay tithes of dill.
You pay tithes of cumin.
But you have neglected the more important matters of the law.
You have neglected justice.
You have neglected mercy.
You have neglected faithfulness.
You should have practiced justice, mercy, and faithfulness.
You should not have neglected tithing either.
passages.original: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί ὅτι ἀποδεκατοῦτε τὸ ἡδύοσμον καὶ τὸ ἄνηθον καὶ τὸ κύμινον καὶ ἀφήκατε τὰ βαρύτερα τοῦ νόμου τὴν κρίσιν καὶ τὸ ἔλεος καὶ τὴν πίστιν ταῦτα δὲ ἔδει ποιῆσαι κἀκεῖνα μὴ ἀφιέναι

passages.text: You blind guides! You strain out a gnat but swallow a camel.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the scribes and Pharisees.
He called them blind guides.
They carefully remove a tiny gnat from their drink.
But they swallow a whole camel.
They focus on small, unimportant things.
But they ignore much bigger, more important matters.
passages.original: ὁδηγοὶ τυφλοί οἱ διϋλίζοντες τὸν κώνωπα τὴν δὲ κάμηλον καταπίνοντες

passages.text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside they are full of greed and self-indulgence.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the scribes and Pharisees.
The scribes and Pharisees were religious leaders.
Jesus called them hypocrites.
He said, “Woe to you.”
You clean the outside of the cup and the dish.
But the inside of the cup and the dish is full of greed.
The inside is also full of self-indulgence.
passages.original: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί ὅτι καθαρίζετε τὸ ἔξωθεν τοῦ ποτηρίου καὶ τῆς παροψίδος ἔσωθεν δὲ γέμουσιν ἐξ ἁρπαγῆς καὶ ἀκρασίας

passages.text: Blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of the cup and dish, so that the outside may become clean as well.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees.
The Pharisees were religious leaders.
The Pharisees acted as guides for the people.
Jesus called the Pharisee blind.
He said, “Blind Pharisee!”
He told the Pharisee to clean the inside of the cup and dish first.
If you clean the inside, the outside will also become clean.
passages.original: Φαρισαῖε τυφλέ καθάρισον πρῶτον τὸ ἐντὸς τοῦ ποτηρίου καὶ τῆς παροψίδος ἵνα γένηται καὶ τὸ ἐκτὸς αὐτοῦ καθαρόν

passages.text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You are like whitewashed tombs, which look beautiful on the outside, but on the inside are full of dead men’s bones and every kind of impurity.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the scribes and Pharisees.
The scribes and Pharisees were religious leaders.
Jesus called them hypocrites.
He warned them with a woe.
He said they were like whitewashed tombs.
Whitewashed tombs look beautiful on the outside.
Inside, these tombs are full of dead men’s bones.
Inside, they are full of every kind of impurity.
passages.original: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί ὅτι παρομοιάζετε τάφοις κεκονιαμένοις οἵτινες ἔξωθεν μὲν φαίνονται ὡραῖοι ἔσωθεν δὲ γέμουσιν ὀστέων νεκρῶν καὶ πάσης ἀκαθαρσίας

passages.text: In the same way, on the outside you appear to be righteous, but on the inside you are full of hypocrisy and wickedness.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the scribes and Pharisees.
He called them hypocrites.
He said they looked righteous to other people on the outside.
He said they appeared good and just to others.
But inside, they were full of hypocrisy.
Inside, they were full of wickedness.
passages.original: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ἔξωθεν μὲν φαίνεσθε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις δίκαιοι ἔσωθεν δέ ἐστε μεστοὶ ὑποκρίσεως καὶ ἀνομίας

passages.text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You build tombs for the prophets and decorate the monuments of the righteous.
passages.sermon:
The scribes and Pharisees are hypocrites.
They build tombs for the prophets.
They decorate the monuments of the righteous.
Woe to them.
passages.original: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί ὅτι οἰκοδομεῖτε τοὺς τάφους τῶν προφητῶν καὶ κοσμεῖτε τὰ μνημεῖα τῶν δικαίων

passages.text: And you say, ‘If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partners with them in shedding the blood of the prophets.’
passages.sermon:
The scribes and Pharisees are hypocrites.
They speak to others.
They say, “If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we would not have joined them.”
They claim they would not have shared in the blood of the prophets.
They say they would not have helped kill God’s prophets.
passages.original: καὶ λέγετε Εἰ ἤμεθα ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν οὐκ ἂν ἤμεθα αὐτῶν κοινωνοὶ ἐν τῷ αἵματι τῶν προφητῶν

passages.text: So you testify against yourselves that you are the sons of those who murdered the prophets.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the scribes and Pharisees.
The scribes and Pharisees were religious leaders.
They were hypocrites.
They claimed they would not have killed the prophets.
But their actions showed the truth.
They gave evidence against themselves.
They proved they were the sons of those who murdered the prophets.
passages.original: ὥστε μαρτυρεῖτε ἑαυτοῖς ὅτι υἱοί ἐστε τῶν φονευσάντων τοὺς προφήτας

passages.text: Fill up, then, the measure of the sin of your fathers.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the religious leaders.
He said they were like their ancestors.
Their ancestors killed the prophets.
Jesus told them to finish what their fathers started.
He told them to fill up the measure of their fathers' sin.
passages.original: καὶ ὑμεῖς πληρώσατε τὸ μέτρον τῶν πατέρων ὑμῶν

passages.text: You snakes! You brood of vipers! How will you escape the sentence of hell?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the religious leaders.
He called them snakes.
He said they were a brood of vipers.
He asked them a question.
He said, “How will you escape the sentence of hell?”
passages.original: ὄφεις γεννήματα ἐχιδνῶν πῶς φύγητε ἀπὸ τῆς κρίσεως τῆς γεέννης

passages.text: Because of this, I am sending you prophets and wise men and teachers. Some of them you will kill and crucify, and others you will flog in your synagogues and persecute in town after town.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people of Jerusalem.
He said, “Because of this, I am sending you prophets.
I am sending you wise men.
I am sending you teachers.
You will kill some of them.
You will crucify some of them.
You will flog others in your synagogues.
You will persecute others from town to town.”
passages.original: Διὰ τοῦτο ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἀποστέλλω πρὸς ὑμᾶς προφήτας καὶ σοφοὺς καὶ γραμματεῖς ἐξ αὐτῶν ἀποκτενεῖτε καὶ σταυρώσετε καὶ ἐξ αὐτῶν μαστιγώσετε ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς ὑμῶν καὶ διώξετε ἀπὸ πόλεως εἰς πόλιν

passages.text: And so upon you will come all the righteous blood shed on earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Berechiah, whom you murdered between the temple and the altar.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people who rejected God's messengers.
He said that judgment would come upon them.
All the righteous blood shed on earth will come upon them.
This includes the blood of Abel.
Abel was righteous.
This also includes the blood of Zechariah.
Zechariah was the son of Berechiah.
They murdered Zechariah between the temple and the altar.
passages.original: ὅπως ἔλθῃ ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς πᾶν αἷμα δίκαιον ἐκχυννόμενον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἀπὸ τοῦ αἵματος Ἅβελ τοῦ δικαίου ἕως τοῦ αἵματος Ζαχαρίου υἱοῦ Βαραχίου ὃν ἐφονεύσατε μεταξὺ τοῦ ναοῦ καὶ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου

passages.text: Truly I tell you, all these things will come upon this generation.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people of Jerusalem.
Jesus said, “Truly, I tell you the truth.
All these things will happen.
These things will come upon this generation.”
passages.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ἥξει ταῦτα πάντα ἐπὶ τὴν γενεὰν ταύτην

passages.text: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her, how often I have longed to gather your children together, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were unwilling!
passages.sermon:
Jerusalem is a city.
Jerusalem kills the prophets.
Jerusalem stones those whom God sends to her.
I am Jesus.
I often wanted to gather your children together.
I wanted to gather them as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings.
You were not willing.
passages.original: Ἰερουσαλὴμ Ἰερουσαλήμ ἡ ἀποκτείνουσα τοὺς προφήτας καὶ λιθοβολοῦσα τοὺς ἀπεσταλμένους πρὸς αὐτήν ποσάκις ἠθέλησα ἐπισυναγαγεῖν τὰ τέκνα σου ὃν τρόπον ὄρνις ἐπισυνάγει τὰ νοσσία αὐτῆς ὑπὸ τὰς πτέρυγας καὶ οὐκ ἠθελήσατε

passages.text: Look, your house is left to you desolate.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people of Jerusalem.
He said, "Look."
Your house is now left to you.
Your house is empty and desolate.
passages.original: ἰδοὺ ἀφίεται ὑμῖν ὁ οἶκος ὑμῶν ἔρημος

passages.text: For I tell you that you will not see Me again until you say, ‘Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.’”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people of Jerusalem.
Jesus said, "You will not see Me again.
You will not see Me from now on.
You will see Me only when you say these words.
You must say, 'Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.'"
Only then will you see Me again.
passages.original: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν οὐ μή με ἴδητε ἀπ’ ἄρτι ἕως ἂν εἴπητε Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου
